stem_book: Inside a uniformly accelerating thin-walled spherical shell of radius R, which is rolling on a horizontal surface, there is a small body slipping around (it stays on the rear side, as shown). Angle of friction between body and inner surface of sphere is 23°. Which of the following can be the acceleration 'a' of the centre of sphere to ensure that the small body stays at R/2 distance from the surface? (a) g/√3 (b) 3g/4 (c) g tan23° (d) g√3/2
reason: added that the body sits on the rear side (figure)
work: body 60° from lowest point; centre frame: shell surface sweeps it up ⇒ friction up; g sin60° − a cos60° = tan23°(g cos60° + a sin60°) ⇒ a = g tan(60° − 23°) = g tan37° = 3g/4
